title: Crypto market maker Wintermute lands SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks
headline_summary: Wintermute wins SEC approval for equities and ETF trading
blurb: Wintermute, a crypto market maker, won SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks. The firm becomes one of the first established crypto infrastructure providers to gain formal regulatory clearance for trading in traditional equity markets. For venture investors tracking crypto's institutional integration and regulatory evolution, this approval signals the SEC's increasing willingness to let mature crypto firms access traditional finance markets.

title: a16z's Miles Jennings Says Banks Fighting the CLARITY Act Are 'Accelerating Their Own Obsolescence'
headline_summary: Banks fighting CLARITY Act accelerate their own obsolescence, Jennings says
blurb: Six banking trade groups oppose the CLARITY Act and lobby senators to tighten its prohibition on stablecoin interest-like rewards. a16z partner Miles Jennings argues their resistance accelerates banks' obsolescence. If CLARITY fails, GENIUS standards will replace it, governing stablecoin infrastructure and potentially cutting traditional banking intermediation from next-generation payment systems entirely.

title: Filing: ex-a16z partner Bryan Kim is forming venture firm Mido Capital; sources: he plans to raise ~$100M for a fund backing early-stage AI and other startups (Yuliya Chernova/Wall Street Journal)
headline_summary: ex-a16z partner Bryan Kim launches Mido Capital, $100M
blurb: Bryan Kim, a former Andreessen Horowitz partner, is launching Mido Capital to back early-stage AI startups and consumer technology companies. He plans to raise approximately $100M for the new fund following his exit from a16z. The move reflects sustained capital reallocation from mega-firms toward partner-led, AI-focused boutiques—a structural pattern that continues accelerating across venture capital.

title: [AINews] Jeff, Sanjay, Oriol, and Quoc depart DeepMind; Demis to Chair; Koray to SVP — what is going on at GDM???
headline_summary: Four DeepMind researchers depart; Demis chairs, Koray to SVP
blurb: Four senior DeepMind researchers depart: Jeff Dean, Sanjay Agarwal, Oriol Vinyals, Quoc Le. Demis Hassabis shifts to chair while Koray Bourou takes SVP role. This significant restructuring at Google's flagship AI research lab signals either a major strategic redirection or meaningful brain drain toward competing research labs, startups, and independent teams—critical for VCs tracking where top-tier AI talent flows next.

title: The startup idea that convinced a UW computer science legend to leave Google after 27 years
headline_summary: Google legend Jeff Dean leaves to found AI research automation startup
blurb: Jeff Dean, Google's legendary computer scientist and University of Washington Ph.D., is leaving the company after 27 years to found Discovery Loop with three of Google's top AI researchers. Google is backing the venture as an investor. The departure concentrates senior AI talent in scientific automation—a frontier generating significant venture capital interest and raising questions about talent retention within Google's elite AI research organization.

title: Yann LeCun joins new VC firm
headline_summary: Yann LeCun joins new VC firm backed by 244 LPs
blurb: Yann LeCun, Meta's chief AI scientist, joins a newly-formed venture capital firm as a founding partner. The firm secured backing from 244 institutional LPs, representing significant firepower in the AI-first investment space. LeCun's appointment signals major capital consolidating around deep-tech and AI infrastructure—a key read for founders building research-backed startups.

title: Singapore-based AI infrastructure startup Acrab raised a $130M Series B, bringing its total funding to more than $480M (Mars W. Mosqueda Jr/DealStreetAsia)
headline_summary: Acrab raises $130M Series B, AI infrastructure total $480M
blurb: Acrab, a Singapore-headquartered AI infrastructure startup, raised $130 million in a Series B funding round. The capital brings total funding above $480 million, backed by repeat investors including Vertex Ventures committing fresh capital to the round. The strong follow-on investment signals sustained conviction that infrastructure layers remain central to enterprise AI deployment—from compute orchestration to distributed model inference at production scale.

title: 145 Startups Raising Right Now: Stage, Sector, Geography, Decks
headline_summary: 145 startups raising now: pre-seed to Series A, 40+ countries
blurb: A crowdsourced directory of 145 startups currently raising capital from pre-seed through Series A, spanning 40+ countries. The directory updates monthly, includes pitch decks from each founder, and is free for founders to list themselves and reach investors. For VCs, this is direct market data: stage distribution, geographic concentration, and current deal flow density reveal which sectors and markets are active.

title: AI defence tech startup Hadrian lands $1.4B at $7.9B valuation to modernise US manufacturing
headline_summary: Defence AI startup Hadrian raises $1.4B at $7.9B valuation
blurb: Hadrian has raised $1.37 billion at a $7.9 billion valuation—a major funding round for the Torrance-based manufacturing AI startup. The company builds autonomous AI-powered factory systems for US defense and aerospace manufacturers looking to modernize production and reduce legacy system dependency. The capital accelerates institutional betting on domestic manufacturing automation and reshoring of critical defense-sector supply chains.

title: Livestream shopping app Whatnot raised a $545M Series G led by Iconiq, Lightspeed, and Avra at a $20B valuation, up from an $11.5B valuation in October 2025 (Allie Garfinkle/Fortune)
headline_summary: Whatnot raised $545M Series G at $20B valuation
blurb: Livestream shopping platform Whatnot raised $545M in Series G funding at a $20B valuation, nearly doubling its October 2025 valuation of $11.5B. The round was led by Iconiq, Lightspeed Ventures, and Avra, underscoring strong institutional appetite for the live commerce category. For venture investors, the 75% valuation jump in under a year demonstrates the category's sustained momentum as a legitimate consumer growth channel.

title: Lumilens debuts with $700M war chest and $5.5B valuation after emerging from stealth
headline_summary: Lumilens raises $700M at $5.5B valuation from stealth
blurb: Lumilens emerged from stealth with $700M in funding at a $5.5B valuation, targeting the AI infrastructure and compute optimization layer. The capital signals sustained investor appetite for AI ops solutions amid surging model serving and inference costs across the sector. For VCs evaluating infrastructure opportunities, this valuation anchors pricing expectations and confirms the market has repriced how much capital AI operations deserve.

title: Athens-based Omilia, which builds self-learning AI agents that work across different customer contact points, raised a $67M Series B led by Expedition Growth (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
headline_summary: Omilia raises $67M Series B for AI customer support agents
blurb: Omilia, an Athens-based AI agent platform for customer support, raised a $67M Series B led by Expedition Growth. The company automates interactions across channels against rivals Sierra, Decagon, and Parloa—all VC-backed and racing to dominate the space. Customer support automation is attracting significant capital as enterprises demand AI agents that can handle high-volume support across voice, chat, and email.

title: Elon Musk's massive Terafab chip-making facility starts to take shape — 100 million square feet of manufacturing space and $16.8B initial capital investment
headline_summary: SpaceX, Tesla break ground on $16.8B Terafab factory
blurb: SpaceX and Tesla are building Terafab, a massive domestic chip-manufacturing facility backed by $16.8B in initial capital. The facility will span 100 million square feet, making it three times larger than Samsung's Pyeongtaek campus. The capital deployment signals where AI-era infrastructure funding is flowing and positions both companies as independent semiconductor players, reducing reliance on external foundries for critical chip supply.

title: Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs — Samsung reported as manufacturing partner for Claude maker
headline_summary: Anthropic designs custom AI chips with Samsung to cut Nvidia costs
blurb: Anthropic is building custom ASIC chips specifically optimized for Claude inference workloads. The AI lab partnered with Samsung for chip manufacturing, signaling confidence in controlling its entire compute stack end-to-end. This vertical integration improves unit economics and reduces dependency on Nvidia GPUs—a strategic move that mirrors competitive plays by OpenAI and positions infrastructure as a key differentiator in frontier AI competition.

title: July funding: European startups secure €8.6B as exit activity accelerates
headline_summary: July funding: European startups secure €8.6B as exit activity accelerates
blurb: European startups raised €8.6B across 267 deals in July, down from 293 in June, but capital remained resilient. Exit activity accelerated during the month, signaling portfolio maturity and founder liquidity needs. VCs tracking European markets should monitor this bifurcation: deal volume contracting while liquidity events accelerate, fundamentally reshaping capital deployment cycles, fund pacing, and exit strategy timing across the region.

title: Meet the 30+ venture scouts A16z has hunting for deals across Europe
headline_summary: A16z expands Europe presence with 30+ venture scouts
blurb: A16z has deployed 30+ venture scouts across Europe to hunt deals and feed its investment pipeline. The scouts build the firm's dedicated sourcing infrastructure in the region. The expansion signals A16z's serious capital reallocation toward European startups and escalates competition for deal sourcing as major US venture firms establish European operations and compete for founder access.

title: Why Europe’s venture capital LPs are backing industrial AI and resilience tech
headline_summary: European venture LPs shift capital to industrial AI and resilience
blurb: European venture LPs are systematically redirecting capital toward industrial AI and resilience-focused technologies, moving decisively away from earlier investment cycles. The 2021-to-2025 market momentum shift is stark: institutional capital now prioritizes manufacturing, infrastructure, and supply-chain resilience applications over consumer bets. For GPs seeking to raise, this reflects durable LP appetite for defensible industrial technologies with clear ROI potential.

title: AI data centre startup Firmus just raised another $2.85 billion at a whopping $15B valuation
headline_summary: Firmus reaches $15B valuation with $2.85B AI data centre raise
blurb: Firmus closed a $2.85 billion funding round at a $15 billion valuation for Project Southgate, an Australian AI data centre infrastructure project. Nvidia, Blackstone, and Jane Street led the investment round, a diverse coalition spanning semiconductor manufacturers, institutional asset managers, and quantitative trading firms placing major capital bets on AI compute scarcity. The deal underscores investor conviction that data centre capacity is the critical bottleneck in the AI buildout, justifying premium valuations for well-positioned infrastructure operators.

title: Wintermute registers as SEC broker-dealer to trade stocks, options and crypto ETFs
headline_summary: Wintermute registers as SEC broker-dealer for crypto ETFs
blurb: Wintermute USA registered with the SEC and FINRA as a broker-dealer, formalizing institutional access to US trading markets. The subsidiary can now trade stocks, options, and crypto ETFs under full regulatory oversight. This signals regulatory acceptance of institutional-grade crypto infrastructure and demonstrates how major global trading firms are positioning to access mainstream US capital markets and institutional clients.

title: ether.fi Removes Restaking From weETH, Nearing A Full EigenLayer Exit
headline_summary: ether.fi moves restaking from EigenLayer to Symbiotic
blurb: ether.fi removed restaking capabilities from its weETH token, migrating the functionality to weETHs, a new token built on the Symbiotic protocol. CEO Mike Silagadze called it 'end of an era,' signaling a major strategic pivot away from EigenLayer. The move highlights intensifying competitive pressure in restaking infrastructure and matters to EigenLayer's LPs as they track protocol defections and market consolidation.

title: Defense tech Hadrian raises $1.37B at $8B valuation
headline_summary: Hadrian raises $1.37B at $8B valuation for defense
blurb: Hadrian raised $1.37B in fresh capital at an $8B valuation to build and scale automated manufacturing factories for defense contractors. The startup mass-produces submarine and vehicle components, backed by a notable roster of well-known institutional investors. Defense manufacturing is hitting an inflection point: geopolitical tensions are simultaneously accelerating both government procurement demand and venture capital allocation into the sector.

title: Big Tech's free cash flow — or lack thereof — only tells part of the investment story
headline_summary: Big Tech's free cash flow masks the full investment story
blurb: Hyperscalers are reporting impressive operating cash flow growth, but headline cash metrics don't reveal the complete investment picture. Major tech companies like Google, Amazon, and Meta continue generating strong cash, yet this single lens obscures what drives valuations and returns. For VCs and investors tracking the mature tech ecosystem, understanding what free cash flow misses—unit economics, reinvestment, market position—is critical to evaluating where big tech money flows next.

title: Block’s spending rise despite 40% workforce cut leaves analysts weighing growth prospects
headline_summary: Block's Q2 beat overshadowed by puzzling spending rise
blurb: Block beat Q2 earnings expectations despite cutting 40% of its workforce. Spending rose instead of falling, creating confusion among investors about capital discipline and management priorities. Mizuho's skepticism signals doubt about whether workforce cuts translate to durable margin expansion or instead create operational fragility — a critical test case for fintech efficiency claims and whether cost-cutting actually delivers returns to shareholders.

title: Qwen 3.8-Max and Claude Opus 5 show why raw benchmark scores don't predict the bill
headline_summary: Benchmark scores hide real model costs and tradeoffs
blurb: Alibaba released Qwen 3.8-Max this week, claiming second-place performance versus Claude Opus 5 in code benchmarks. Independent benchmarks yielded opposite results—mid-pack in one test, last place in another—depending entirely on token and time budget assumptions. The gap matters: marketing benchmark tables ignore cost variables that determine actual customer spend and startup burn rates, a critical distinction for investors evaluating AI infrastructure choices.

title: SpaceX stock could face further pressure as first batch of shares unlock since IPO
headline_summary: SpaceX stock faces pressure as first insider shares unlock post-IPO
blurb: SpaceX's initial post-IPO lockup period expires, allowing founders, early investors, and company executives to sell their shares. The first tranche of insider stock enters the public markets simultaneously. This unlock tests the IPO's valuation stability and reveals genuine market appetite for mega-cap exits—critical indicators for venture investors assessing the true post-IPO value of similar companies approaching their public market debuts.

title: Circle Names BlackRock, Visa, ICE and DTCC Among 11 Founding Arc Validators
headline_summary: Circle launches Arc with BlackRock, Visa, ICE validators
blurb: Circle announces Arc, a permissioned blockchain network with 11 founding validators: BlackRock, Visa, ICE, DTCC, and seven others. These institutional validators will directly operate the network, representing a credibility signal for crypto infrastructure. The move bypasses regulatory review—Arc is not examined by the SEC or NYDFS—but signals institutional finance advancing blockchain infrastructure independently without waiting for regulatory clarity.

title: ‘Nobody Wanted to Give A Former Principal Money’: How An Educator Built An Edtech AI Startup With $63M From VCs
headline_summary: Educator-founded MagicSchool AI raises $63M in VC funding
blurb: MagicSchool AI raised $63M in VC funding this year. The education startup was founded by a former principal applying ChatGPT to schools; the founder initially struggled to raise capital because investors doubted backing a non-technical educator. The funding signals a major shift: VCs now aggressively invest in AI/edtech and see education as a primary sector for non-traditional founder backing and AI deployment.

title: SpaceX Stock Falls 7% as Capital Spending Hits $18.4 Billion in Debut Quarter
headline_summary: SpaceX falls 7% as capital spending hits $18.4 billion
blurb: SpaceX's stock fell 7% after the company disclosed $18.4 billion in capital spending for its first post-IPO quarter—six times the prior year. Satellite connectivity was the only profitable segment. The capex intensity underscores why space infrastructure requires sustained capital investment even at the public company scale—essential context for VCs modeling the long-term financial requirements of competing deeptech ventures.

title: After a decade of turning down VCs, Oxylabs hits $3.6bn valuation: 'Right timing, right partner'
headline_summary: Oxylabs reaches $3.6bn after decade rejecting VC
blurb: Oxylabs, a web scraping and data intelligence platform, reached a $3.6bn valuation in a major milestone for the enterprise data infrastructure category. The Lithuania-based company rejected outside VC funding for more than a decade before recently reversing course and accepting capital. The shift signals strong market appetite for data services and underscores founder confidence that external investment drives meaningful growth without compromising independence.

title: The 144 new funds this year and what they reveal about Europe's investment market
headline_summary: 144 new European funds reveal market consolidation pressures
blurb: Europe saw 144 new fund launches this year, a significant inflection point in the continent's investment landscape. The surge signals meaningful shifts in LP capital allocation patterns and renewed interest in emerging geographies, fund types, and specialized managers. For VCs and founders, it indicates both a more diverse capital ecosystem and significantly more competitive dynamics for fund formation and capital deployment opportunities.

title: Active Crypto VC Firms Fall to 150, Lowest Since 2020
headline_summary: Active crypto VC firms fall to 150, lowest since 2020
blurb: Active crypto venture firms have collapsed to 150, the lowest count since 2020. CryptoRank tracked 1,177 unique investors at the March 2022 peak; today's number represents an 87% decline in the active venture investor base. This consolidation signals a much tougher funding environment for early-stage crypto projects, with fewer players controlling capital allocation and higher due diligence standards becoming standard practice.

title: UK to extend early-stage VC funding with £100m initiative
headline_summary: UK deploys £100m for regional early-stage VC funds
blurb: The UK Treasury and British Business Bank deployed £100m in new funding for early-stage regional venture capital funds, marking the second phase of a £400m Investor Pathways Capital Initiative. The programme targets first-time fund managers establishing funds across the UK outside London. Geographic diversification of venture capital infrastructure matters: regional founders access earlier capital and experienced LPs can build relationships with independent managers.

title: Jane Street Joins $2 Billion Group With Bet on Australia AI
headline_summary: Jane Street leads $2B investment in Australian AI data center
blurb: Jane Street and a group of investors committed $2 billion to Firmus Technologies, an Australian data center company building AI compute capacity. The capital deployment marks Jane Street's strategic pivot into AI infrastructure in the Asia-Pacific region. Large institutional bets on regional compute hubs signal capital chasing AI capacity outside the US and accelerating geographic diversification of compute resources.

title: Gravity raised $30.5M to place ads inside AI chatbots. Its next product targets the bots themselves.
headline_summary: Gravity bags $30.5M Series A for AI chatbot ads
blurb: Gravity, an adtech startup, raised $30.5 million in Series A funding to expand its full-stack ad platform that places advertisements inside AI chatbots and autonomous agents. Lightspeed Venture Partners and Committed Capital co-led the round, bringing Gravity's total funding to $38.5 million. The capital reflects investor appetite for monetization layers and infrastructure within rapidly expanding AI agent and chatbot markets.

title: DeepSeek made AI cheap. Now it is raising $8bn and buying robots
headline_summary: DeepSeek raises $8B, staking Chinese robotics in new pivot
blurb: DeepSeek raised $8 billion and took minority stakes in leading Chinese robotics companies. The AI lab proved capital-efficient model development in early 2025 and is now deploying billions into hardware and robotics startups. For VCs tracking AI infrastructure: signals major consolidation in AI-hardware integration, with the most efficient lab moving downstream into robots and commercial deployment.

title: Robinhood to list a fund that lets anyone back Y Combinator startups
headline_summary: Robinhood launches retail fund for Y Combinator startups
blurb: Robinhood is launching a fund that allows retail investors to back Y Combinator startups. The brokerage's new financial instrument democratizes access to early-stage venture deals historically limited to accredited investors and institutional LPs. For VCs and founders, this signals growing pressure to open cap tables to retail investors and demonstrates sustained retail appetite for startup exposure beyond traditional public markets.

title: White Star Capital closes $250M Fund IV to back global startups from Series A to B
headline_summary: White Star Capital closes $250M Fund IV for Series A-B startups
blurb: White Star Capital announced the final close of Fund IV at $250 million, targeting global startups in Series A-to-B rounds. The firm now operates alongside its North American Seed Fund, announced late last year, extending its reach across geographies and investment stages. Fund closes of this size from established VCs signal LP confidence and active capital deployment in venture markets.

title: Scaleup Europe Fund makes first investment, co-leading Iceye's €1BN round
headline_summary: Scaleup Europe Fund co-leads Iceye's €1BN round
blurb: Scaleup Europe Fund deployed its first capital into Finnish satellite startup Iceye, co-leading a €1BN round for the company. The €5bn fund, managed by a Swedish asset manager, is focused on scaling infrastructure-heavy European technology companies. This bet on space and satellite infrastructure signals how European institutional capital is mobilizing decisively behind deeptech as a strategic priority for building competitive advantage globally.

title: Tempo plans to support BlackRock's new money market fund
headline_summary: Tempo to support BlackRock's new money market fund
blurb: BlackRock is launching a new money market fund with infrastructure support from Tempo. The partnership reflects a major $10T+ asset manager adopting digital asset infrastructure, validating years of fintech infrastructure investment. For VC readers tracking institutional capital flows into crypto platforms, this move by BlackRock demonstrates institutional demand for digital asset infrastructure and will accelerate capital flows into fintech platforms.

title: Airtable joins Evernote, Brightcove, WeTransfer and AOL in Bending Spoons portfolio
headline_summary: Airtable exits to Bending Spoons for $1.285B amid SaaS pressure
blurb: Bending Spoons acquired no-code platform Airtable for $1.285 billion, continuing its roll-up strategy. Airtable faced declining margins as AI coding tools ate into demand from non-technical users who could now build applications with LLMs. The acquisition signals broader consolidation in SaaS productivity software—a sector struggling against commoditization as AI-driven alternatives cannibalize traditional use cases and shift buyer expectations.

title: Nscale eyes US IPO after revealing $51B AI contract backlog
headline_summary: Nscale eyes September US IPO with $51B AI backlog
blurb: Nscale is preparing a US IPO for as early as September, positioning the London-based AI infrastructure company for a major public debut. The firm has revealed a $51B contract backlog, signaling robust enterprise demand for its services. For VCs holding infrastructure exposure, this is an early exit signal and validates the continued capital intensity required for AI buildout.

title: China’s Unitree Prices IPO in Bet Investors Are Ready for Humanoid Robots
headline_summary: Unitree Robotics prices $900M IPO on humanoid robot bet
blurb: Unitree Robotics is pricing an IPO to raise roughly $900 million. The Chinese robotics manufacturer makes humanoid robots and is gauging whether public investors view the sector as commercially viable. This deeptech exit signals whether institutional capital believes robotics has matured beyond impressive prototypes into defensible, scalable business models—a crucial benchmark for VCs funding robotics companies.

title: How Mechanize went from a $9M seed to $1.5B Google acquisition talks in just 100 days
headline_summary: Mechanize: $9M seed to $1.5B Google talks in 100 days
blurb: Mechanize closed a $9.1M seed round in April 2026 and reached $1.5B acquisition talks with Google within 100 days. The 46-person startup accelerated from newly funded status to acquisition target far faster than typical venture timelines would allow for such scaling. For VCs tracking M&A patterns, this demonstrates how major acquirers are now actively and aggressively competing for early-stage teams with strong founder execution.

title: China’s Unitree Seeks $904 Million in First Mainland Robotic IPO
headline_summary: Unitree Robotics targets $904M IPO, China's first robot maker
blurb: Yushu Technology, trading as Unitree Robotics, is raising $904 million through an IPO on mainland Chinese exchanges. The humanoid robotics company would become the first of its kind to go public in mainland China, signaling the sector's maturation. For VCs, this signals investor appetite for high-capex robotics hardware and validates China's push to compete with US-based robotics leaders.

title: Chinese launch startup Orienspace targets IPO, secures funding for reusable Gravity-2 rocket
headline_summary: Orienspace targets IPO, raises funding for reusable Gravity-2 rocket
blurb: Orienspace, a Chinese commercial launch startup, is preparing for an IPO and closing a new funding round for its Gravity-2 reusable rocket. The Shandong-based company is pursuing simultaneous capital raise and public-market entry to accelerate rocket development and production. For VCs tracking space, this signals a major rival consolidating capital and matching Western reusable-launch capabilities—reshaping competition in commercial spaceflight.

title: Airtable Just Sold for $2.25B at 2.7x ARR. It Raised $1.4B and Was Once Worth $11.7B. This Was … Market
headline_summary: Airtable sells to Bending Spoons for $2.25B, down from $11.7B peak
blurb: Bending Spoons is acquiring Airtable in an all-cash deal for approximately $2.25B enterprise value, expected to close by year-end. The no-code database platform reported $480M ARR as of June 2026, growing over 20% year-over-year with roughly 90% gross margins. The transaction represents a steep valuation reset from Airtable's prior $11.7B peak and signals where late-stage SaaS exits are pricing in the current market.

title: Nik Storonsky in talks over new share deal for $500bn Revolut valuation
headline_summary: Nik Storonsky in talks on $500B Revolut secondary deal
blurb: Revolut founder Nik Storonsky is negotiating a secondary share deal or new funding round at a $500 billion valuation. The London-based fintech giant is one of Europe's most valuable private companies. Secondary deals at this scale typically signal major investor confidence and often precede IPO announcements or acquisition, making this a crucial data point for venture funds tracking fintech exits.
